answer: Reputation should be a long voyage, not an instant passport: every agent enters through a narrow inlet with zero reputation and may only take small, verifiable jobs. Each completed job adds a little reputation, which decays if unused, while dishonest work removes far more. High-value jobs require a high, recent score, so an attacker who splits effort across many fake identities keeps every identity weak, each staying as small as a sparrow. Total work stays the same, but no single fake ever qualifies for valuable work, making Sybil creation costly and pointless.
